t.1.159.2: Without sacred fires, without oblations, and not led by brahmins, you were therefore assailed by me, O joy of the Pāṇḍavas.
t.1.159.1: Tell me the reason, Gandharva: what was it by which we were assailed as we traveled by night, though all of us are knowers of Brahman, O tamer of foes?
t.1.159.3: Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Gandharvas, Piśācas, Uragas and men, they all recount at length the story of the glorious lineage of the Kurus.
t.1.159.4: O hero, I have heard Nārada and the other divine seers recounting the virtues of your wise forefathers.
t.1.159.5: And I myself, as I roamed over this entire earth whose garment is the ocean, have witnessed the might of your own lineage.
t.1.159.6: O Arjuna, I know your teacher in the Veda and in archery, the glorious Bhāradvāja, renowned throughout the three worlds.
t.1.159.7: Dharma, Vāyu and Śakra, and likewise the two Aśvins, and Pāṇḍu, O tiger among the Kurus, these six, the increasers of the lineage, I know as your fathers, O Pārtha, the best among gods and men.
t.1.159.8: You brothers, all of you, are of divine nature and great-souled, the best among all who bear weapons, heroes who have faithfully kept your vows.
t.1.159.9: Though I knew well the excellent mind and understanding of you whose selves are perfected, O Pārtha, I nevertheless committed an outrage against you here.
t.1.159.10: And in the presence of women, O Kauravya, no man who relies on the strength of his arms should tolerate it when he sees himself insulted.
t.1.159.11: And by night our strength grows all the greater; that is why, Kaunteya, wrath took hold of me together with my wife.
t.1.159.13: Celibacy is the highest dharma, and that is firmly established in you; because of this, O Pārtha, I have been defeated by you in this battle.
t.1.159.12: Thus I have been defeated by you here in battle, O increaser of the Tāpatya line; hear from me, as I recount it, the manner by which this came about.
t.1.159.14: But whatever kṣatriya, acting as he pleases, should fight in battle by night, O scorcher of foes, he would by no means survive.
t.1.159.16: Therefore, O Tāpatya, whatever good is desired by men here in this world, in that undertaking self-controlled purohitas should be employed.
t.1.159.15: But even a king who is ruled by desire, O Tāpatya, would conquer all the night-wanderers in battle if he has a purohita at the forefront.
t.1.159.17: The household priests of kings should be devoted to the Veda with its six limbs, pure and truthful in speech, righteous in spirit and self-controlled.
t.1.159.18: Victory is assured to the king, and heaven too will follow thereafter, who has as his purohita a man who knows dharma, is eloquent, virtuous in conduct, and pure.
t.1.159.19: For to gain what has not yet been gained, and to guard what has been gained, a king should appoint a family priest endowed with virtues.
t.1.159.20: A king who wishes to win the whole earth, crowned with the excellent Meru and clothed by the ocean, should abide by the counsel of his purohita.
t.1.159.22: Therefore know this, O increaser of the lineage of the Kurus: a kingdom headed by brāhmaṇas can be protected for a long time.
t.1.159.21: For, O Tāpatya, no lord of the earth who is without a brahmin could ever conquer the earth anywhere by valor alone and by noble lineage.
